task_description: Skill-guided evaluation of the correct Maestro BPMN debug workflow against a mocked `uip` CLI. The agent debugs an existing local project with inputs, captures the instance id the debug command returns, then inspects the run via the `debug-instance` commands and summarizes the runtime variable values. The summary values are only discoverable from the mocked CLI JSON, so a prose guess cannot pass. No cloud side effects — the CLI is backed by a local fixture harness.

1	# Operate - Package, ship, run, and manage BPMN processes
2	
3	Capability index for BPMN Process Orchestration lifecycle work. Operate owns the steps that prepare a BPMN project
4	for the cloud and the steps that touch the cloud: package generation, Studio Web upload, Orchestrator publish/deploy,
5	debug/run, job inspection, and instance lifecycle.
6	These actions may contact UiPath services or external systems.
7	
8	> **Where you came from / where to go next.** Operate is downstream of Author (model-authored BPMN plus CLI
9	> validation/enrichment) and upstream of Diagnose (runtime faults and state inspection).
10	> BPMN source work lives in [registry-workflow.md](../registry-workflow.md);
11	> post-run investigation lives in [diagnose/CAPABILITY.md](../diagnose/CAPABILITY.md).
12	>
13	> **Inherits universal rules from [SKILL.md](../../SKILL.md).** In particular: BPMN XML is source, generated package
14	> files and Integration Service enrichment are CLI-owned, parsed CLI output uses `--output json`, and
15	> upload/publish/deploy/debug/run/lifecycle actions require explicit user consent.
16	
17	## When to use this capability
18	
19	- Package a Maestro BPMN Process Orchestration project.
20	- Upload a project to Studio Web.
21	- Publish or deploy a packaged process when explicitly requested.
22	- Debug or run a process instance after explicit consent.
23	- Inspect jobs, processes, process versions, instances, variables, incidents, and traces.
24	- Pause, resume, cancel, retry, migrate, or move a running instance when explicitly requested.
25	- Refresh or regenerate CLI-owned package metadata before a cloud action.
26	
27	## Critical rules
28	
29	1. **Never debug or run without explicit consent** - execution can call connectors, start child processes, create Action
30	   Center work, mutate queues, send messages, or update external systems.
31	2. **Ask before every cloud-side mutation** - upload, publish, deploy, debug, process run, pause, resume, cancel, retry,
32	   migrate, and cursor movement require a clear user decision for that action.
33	3. **Validate before operate** - do not upload, publish, debug, or run until Author validation is complete or the user
34	   explicitly accepts known draft warnings.
35	4. **Refresh or regenerate package metadata before cloud actions** - run `uip maestro bpmn update-metadata <file.bpmn> --dry-run` to check drift, then `uip maestro bpmn update-metadata <file.bpmn>` to regenerate. Stale `bindings_v2.json`, `entry-points.json`,
36	   `operate.json`, or `package-descriptor.json` can break import or runtime even when the BPMN source is correct.
37	5. **Keep source and package ownership clear** - fix process structure, variables, mappings, events, and documented non-IS
38	   extensions in `.bpmn`; rerun CLI generation/enrichment for generated package JSON and Integration Service metadata.
39	6. **Default publish wording to Studio Web upload unless the user explicitly asks for Orchestrator deployment** - keep deploy semantics explicit.
40	7. **Always include folder context on runtime commands that require it** - `process run` takes `<FOLDER_KEY>` and
41	   `instance`/`incident get` commands require `--folder-key` or `-f`.
42	8. **Report identifiers plainly** - summarize returned Studio Web URLs, package paths, solution IDs, process keys,
43	   job keys, instance IDs, run IDs, final status, and folder context when available.
44	9. **Do not retry before diagnosis** - identify root cause first, then decide whether retry, cancel, migrate,
45	   cursor movement, or source repair is appropriate.
46	
47	## Workflow
48	
49	| Journey | Read |
50	| --- | --- |
51	| Package and upload or publish | [references/ship.md](references/ship.md) |
52	| Debug/run and inspect execution | [references/run.md](references/run.md) |
53	| Manage a running instance | [references/manage.md](references/manage.md) |
54	
55	## Common tasks
56	
57	| I need to... | Read these |
58	| --- | --- |
59	| Prepare for Studio Web upload | [references/ship.md](references/ship.md), [shared/project-layout.md](../shared/project-layout.md) |
60	| Deploy to Orchestrator | [references/ship.md](references/ship.md) |
61	| Run/debug a BPMN process | [references/run.md](references/run.md) |
62	| Inspect job or instance status | [references/run.md](references/run.md) |
63	| Pause/resume/cancel/retry | [references/manage.md](references/manage.md) |
64	| Migrate or move an instance cursor | [references/manage.md](references/manage.md) |
65	| Correlate a running instance to deployed BPMN | [diagnose/CAPABILITY.md](../diagnose/CAPABILITY.md) |
66	| Diagnose a failed run | [diagnose/CAPABILITY.md](../diagnose/CAPABILITY.md) |
67	
68	## Anti-patterns
69	
70	- **Never treat package generation as source authoring** - generated files reflect BPMN plus enrichment.
71	- **Never upload a draft with unresolved Integration Service enrichment unless the user explicitly wants a non-executable
72	  draft review.**
73	- **Never run lifecycle commands just to validate XML.**
74	- **Never default to Orchestrator deploy when the user says "publish."** Use Studio Web upload unless the target is explicit.
75	- **Never use `debug` as a substitute for validation.** Debug executes the process against real services.
76	- **Never retry a faulted instance without checking incidents and deployed asset correlation.**
77	
78	## References
79	
80	### Operate-scoped
81	
82	- [ship.md](references/ship.md) - package, upload, publish, deploy
83	- [run.md](references/run.md) - debug, run, status, traces
84	- [manage.md](references/manage.md) - pause, resume, cancel, retry, migrate, cursor movement
85	
86	### Cross-capability
87	
88	- [shared/project-layout.md](../shared/project-layout.md) - package files and content
89	- [shared/cli-conventions.md](../cli-conventions.md) - side effects, login, JSON output
90	- [author/validation.md](../structural-bpmn.md) - pre-operate validation
91	- [diagnose/CAPABILITY.md](../diagnose/CAPABILITY.md) - failure investigation

1	# Diagnose - Investigate failed BPMN runs
2	
3	Capability index for post-run investigation.
4	Diagnose owns the diagnostic priority ladder for BPMN Process Orchestration runs: incidents, runtime variables,
5	deployed BPMN asset correlation, element executions, cursors, generated package metadata, and traces.
6	
7	> **Where you came from / where to go next.** Diagnose is downstream of Operate (a debug or deployed run failed, hung,
8	> or behaved unexpectedly) and points back to Author for source fixes.
9	> Running and lifecycle live in [operate/CAPABILITY.md](../operate/CAPABILITY.md);
10	> source fixes live in [registry-workflow.md](../registry-workflow.md).
11	>
12	> **Inherits universal rules from [SKILL.md](../../SKILL.md).** BPMN source is model-authored; generated package files
13	> and Integration Service enrichment are CLI-owned.
14	> Use `uip maestro bpmn ... --output json` for diagnostic reads and redact private runtime data in summaries.
15	
16	## When to use this capability
17	
18	- Triage a failed debug or deployed process run.
19	- Read incidents and faulting element IDs.
20	- Inspect runtime variables and element executions.
21	- Fetch the deployed BPMN asset when local files may differ.
22	- Map runtime failures back to BPMN source and generated package metadata.
23	- Identify failures caused by unresolved Integration Service enrichment, bad bindings, missing diagrams, invalid mappings,
24	  or stale package files.
25	- Decide whether the safe next action is retry, cancel, migrate, cursor movement, re-authoring, package regeneration,
26	  or cloud configuration repair.
27	
28	## Critical rules
29	
30	1. **Investigate in priority order** - context, incidents, runtime variables, deployed BPMN asset,
31	   element executions/cursors, generated package files, then traces. For failed
32	   BPMN run triage, always execute the deployed asset read
33	   `uip maestro bpmn instance asset <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json`
34	   before writing the diagnosis, even when incidents and variables already
35	   reveal the likely root cause.
36	2. **Always include folder context on instance and incident reads** - `instance` commands require `--folder-key` or `-f`,
37	   and `incident get` requires `--folder-key`.
38	3. **Use the CLI as the diagnostic interface** - run `uip maestro bpmn ... --output json` reads. When mock or fixture
39	   files are present in a test harness, treat them as CLI backing data and do not read those files directly unless you
40	   are explicitly debugging the mock harness.
41	4. **Fetch deployed BPMN when local source may differ** - do not assume the working tree matches what ran.
42	5. **Map failures to BPMN element IDs** - use IDs to identify the source node, gateway, event, sequence flow,
43	   or extension that needs Author work.
44	6. **Separate runtime symptoms from ownership of the fix** - BPMN structure and mappings belong in Author;
45	   Integration Service enrichment and generated JSON come from CLI generation;
46	   folder/process/release choices belong to cloud configuration.
47	7. **Do not expose private runtime data** - redact tenant, user, connection, folder, URL, payload,
48	   and secret values in summaries.
49	8. **Do not mutate while diagnosing** - retry, cancel, migrate, and cursor movement are Operate actions and require
50	   explicit user consent after root cause analysis.
51	
52	## Workflow
53	
54	| Journey | Read |
55	| --- | --- |
56	| Triage a failed run | [references/troubleshooting-guide.md](references/troubleshooting-guide.md) |
57	| Recognize recurring failure patterns | [references/failure-modes.md](references/failure-modes.md) |
58	
59	## Common tasks
60	
61	| I need to... | Read these |
62	| --- | --- |
63	| Find the faulting element | [references/troubleshooting-guide.md](references/troubleshooting-guide.md) |
64	| Compare local and deployed BPMN | [references/troubleshooting-guide.md](references/troubleshooting-guide.md) |
65	| Inspect runtime variables, cursors, or element executions | [references/troubleshooting-guide.md](references/troubleshooting-guide.md) |
66	| Diagnose binding or generated JSON issues | [failure modes](references/failure-modes.md), [project layout](../shared/project-layout.md) |
67	| Diagnose Integration Service runtime issues | [failure modes](references/failure-modes.md) |
68	| Decide whether retry is safe | [troubleshooting guide](references/troubleshooting-guide.md), [manage guide](../operate/references/manage.md) |
69	| Fix the source | [registry-workflow.md](../registry-workflow.md) |
70	
71	For Integration Service enrichment details, read
72	[registry-workflow.md](../registry-workflow.md).
73	
74	## Anti-patterns
75	
76	- **Never start with verbose traces when incidents are available.**
77	- **Never call runtime lifecycle commands while diagnosing.** Diagnose reads; Operate mutates after explicit consent.
78	- **Never assume local BPMN is the deployed asset.**
79	- **Never retry before root cause is known.**
80	- **Never paste private incident payloads or connection details into docs, commits, or issue comments.**
81	- **Never patch generated package files as the only fix for a BPMN source defect.**
82	
83	## References
84	
85	### Diagnose-scoped
86	
87	- [troubleshooting-guide.md](references/troubleshooting-guide.md) - diagnostic priority ladder
88	- [failure-modes.md](references/failure-modes.md) - recurring failure patterns
89	
90	### Cross-capability
91	
92	- [shared/bpmn-xml-contract.md](../structural-bpmn.md) - XML authoring and validation boundaries
93	- [shared/project-layout.md](../shared/project-layout.md) - generated files and package shape
94	- [shared/variables-bindings-expressions.md](../expression-authoring.md) - mappings and binding expressions
95	- [shared/public-safety.md](../public-safety.md) - redaction and sanitization

1	# Run - Debug, process run, and status inspection
2	
3	Use this journey to debug or run a BPMN Process Orchestration project and inspect execution status.
4	Debug and deployed process runs are side-effecting operations.
5	Status, incidents, variables, and deployed-asset reads are inspection operations.
6	
7	## Consent gate
8	
9	Before any debug or process run:
10	
11	- Explain that execution can call connectors, start child processes, create human tasks, mutate queues, send messages,
12	  or update external systems.
13	- Confirm input arguments and target folder/context.
14	- Confirm the project has passed validation and required CLI-owned enrichment.
15	- Ask for explicit consent for this run. Prior consent for upload, validation, or packaging is not consent to execute.
16	
17	## Debug - controlled Studio Web run
18	
19	Use debug when the user wants to upload a local BPMN project to Studio Web and run a debug session with full Studio Web
20	visibility.
21	
22	For local project debug, prefer a solution context so generated resources,
23	bindings, and debug metadata are available. Initialize a solution, import the
24	BPMN project, refresh resources, and run debug from the solution directory:
25	
26	```bash
27	uip solution init <SolutionName> --output json
28	uip solution projects import --source <ProjectDir> --solutionFile <SolutionName>/<SolutionName>.uipx --output json
29	uip solution resources refresh --solution-folder <SolutionName> --output json
30	cd <SolutionName> && uip maestro bpmn debug <ProjectDirName> --output json
31	```
32	
33	```bash
34	uip maestro bpmn debug [project-path] --output json
35	```
36	
37	Pass input arguments only after confirming the values and redacting secrets from summaries:
38	
39	```bash
40	uip maestro bpmn debug [project-path] --inputs @inputs.json --output json
41	```
42	
43	If a target folder is needed, provide the folder ID exposed by the CLI:
44	
45	```bash
46	uip maestro bpmn debug [project-path] --folder-id <FOLDER_ID> --output json
47	```
48	
49	Parse and report returned identifiers such as `Data.jobKey`, `Data.instanceId`, `Data.runId`, `Data.solutionId`,
50	and `Data.finalStatus`.
51	If Studio Web URL is not returned, print `Studio Web URL: <not returned by CLI>`.
52	
53	> **The debug command output has element statuses, not variable values.** Its
54	> element-execution list reports each element's status (Completed/Faulted) but
55	> never the runtime *values*. A Completed final status with all elements green
56	> proves the process ran — NOT that any output variable holds the expected value.
57	> To inspect runtime variable definitions and any values the runtime exposes,
58	> take the returned instance id and run
59	> `uip maestro bpmn debug-instance variables-all <INSTANCE_ID> --output json`
60	> (below). Debug instances are ephemeral — read variables in the same session,
61	> right after the debug run. Match returned keys case-insensitively
62	> (`finalStatus`/`FinalStatus`, `instanceId`/`InstanceId`, `elementExecutions`/
63	> `ElementExecutions`) — the CLI's JSON key casing varies by version.
64	
65	## Process run - deployed process
66	
67	Use process run only for a process already deployed to Orchestrator.
68	
69	```bash
70	uip maestro bpmn process list --output json
71	uip maestro bpmn process get <PROCESS_KEY> <FEED_ID> --output json
72	uip maestro bpmn process run <PROCESS_KEY> <FOLDER_KEY> --inputs @inputs.json --validate --output json
73	```
74	
75	`process run` requires the folder key as a positional argument.
76	Use `--release-key`, `--feed-id`, or `--robot-ids` only when the user provides those deployment-specific choices
77	or the process discovery output clearly identifies them.
78	
79	## Job and instance inspection
80	
81	Use status first, then incidents and variables if the status is faulted or ambiguous:
82	
83	```bash
84	uip maestro bpmn job status <JOB_KEY> --folder-key <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
85	uip maestro bpmn instance get <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
86	uip maestro bpmn instance incidents <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
87	```
88	
89	Use traces only when status, incidents, variables, and deployed BPMN correlation are insufficient:
90	
91	```bash
92	uip maestro bpmn job traces <JOB_KEY> --output json
93	```
94	
95	For debug instances, prefer the `debug-instance` inspection commands when
96	standard deployed-instance commands do not have debug-session context. Use the
97	identifiers returned by the debug command as the source of truth.
98	
99	```bash
100	uip maestro bpmn debug-instance incidents <INSTANCE_ID> --output json
101	uip maestro bpmn debug-instance variables <INSTANCE_ID> --output json
102	uip maestro bpmn debug-instance variables-all <INSTANCE_ID> --output json
103	```
104	
105	## Execution summary
106	
107	When a run starts, report:
108	
109	- Studio Web URL, if returned.
110	- Process key, job key, run ID, solution ID, or instance ID, if returned.
111	- Folder/context, if known.
112	- Input summary, with secrets redacted.
113	- Final status if the command waited for completion.
114	- Next inspection command or status path.
115	
116	When the user cares about a business result, final status alone is insufficient.
117	Also report the relevant output variable definition and any value the API
118	returns. Current BPMN live debug can expose a root output definition while
119	returning that computed root output value as `null`; call out that
120	runtime/debug API limitation when you see it.
121	
122	## Status and traces
123	
124	Start with status and incidents before verbose traces.
125	Traces can be large and should be pulled only when incidents and variables are insufficient.
126	
127	If execution faults, hand off to [diagnose/CAPABILITY.md](../../diagnose/CAPABILITY.md).
128	
129	## Anti-patterns
130	
131	- **Never run `uip maestro bpmn debug` as validation.** Use Author validation and packaging checks for correctness;
132	  debug executes the process.
133	- **Never reuse stale inputs silently.** Confirm every side-effecting run's input set and redact secrets from summaries.
134	- **Never skip folder context for deployed runs.** `process run` requires `<FOLDER_KEY>` and instance inspection commands
135	  require `--folder-key` or `-f`.
136	- **Never start diagnosis from traces.** Use incidents, variables, deployed BPMN asset, and element executions first.

1	# Troubleshooting Guide
2	
3	Use this priority ladder for failed or misbehaving BPMN runs.
4	
5	> **Read-only boundary:** this guide diagnoses.
6	> Retry, cancel, migrate, and cursor movement are Operate actions and require explicit user consent after root cause is known.
7	>
8	> **Folder context:** `uip maestro bpmn instance ...` commands require `--folder-key <FOLDER_KEY>` or
9	> `-f <FOLDER_KEY>`.
10	> `uip maestro bpmn incident get` requires `--folder-key <FOLDER_KEY>`.
11	
12	## Step 1 - Confirm context
13	
14	Collect public-safe identifiers:
15	
16	- Process or package name.
17	- Instance/job ID.
18	- Folder/context label.
19	- Approximate run time.
20	- Local commit or package version, if known.
21	- Whether the run came from `uip maestro bpmn debug` or `uip maestro bpmn process run`.
22	
23	Do not record secrets, tenant URLs, connection IDs, or payload data in public notes.
24	
25	If you only have a deployed-process job key, start with:
26	
27	```bash
28	uip maestro bpmn job status <JOB_KEY> --folder-key <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
29	```
30	
31	Parse the instance ID, folder context, process key, final status, and any trace/run identifiers from the JSON output.
32	For debug runs, prefer the `instanceId` returned by
33	`uip maestro bpmn debug` and inspect it with `debug-instance` commands. Keep
34	deployed-instance status reads and debug-session inspection separate.
35	
36	## Step 2 - Read incidents
37	
38	Find the incident category, message, and faulting BPMN element ID.
39	If multiple incidents exist, start with the first root fault and avoid chasing downstream cancellation noise.
40	
41	```bash
42	uip maestro bpmn instance incidents <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
43	uip maestro bpmn incident get <INCIDENT_ID> --folder-key <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
44	uip maestro bpmn incident summary --output json
45	```
46	
47	For process-level incident overview:
48	
49	```bash
50	uip maestro bpmn processes incidents <PROCESS_KEY> --output json
51	```
52	
53	## Step 3 - Inspect runtime variables
54	
55	Inspect variables around the faulting element.
56	Redact private payloads.
57	Check whether expected outputs were missing, malformed, or literal strings instead of evaluated expressions.
58	If the user reports a behavioral mismatch, inspect variables even when the final
59	run status is `Completed`; a completed run only proves control-flow completion,
60	not semantic correctness.
61	
62	```bash
63	uip maestro bpmn instance variables <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
64	uip maestro bpmn instance variables <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --parent-element-id <ELEMENT_ID> --output json
65	```
66	
67	For affected elements, confirm runtime inputs and outputs match the modeled
68	contract before changing source.
69	
70	## Step 4 - Correlate deployed BPMN
71	
72	Fetch the deployed BPMN asset when local source may differ. Compare:
73	
74	- Faulting element ID.
75	- Root variables and mappings.
76	- Binding expressions.
77	- Integration Service extension content.
78	- Diagram and sequence-flow structure when the failure is import or package related.
79	
80	```bash
81	uip maestro bpmn instance asset <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
82	```
83	
84	For failed-run triage, always run this deployed asset command before the final
85	diagnosis, even when earlier incident and variable reads already explain the
86	failure. The deployed asset proves which BPMN definition actually ran and keeps
87	the priority ladder observable in command logs.
88	
89	Use the incident's faulting element ID to locate the BPMN element in the deployed asset first, then compare to local
90	`.bpmn`.
91	If they differ, diagnose what actually ran and treat local edits as a future fix, not as the executed definition.
92	
93	## Step 5 - Inspect element executions and cursors
94	
95	Element executions and cursors show where the runtime moved before it faulted or hung:
96	
97	```bash
98	uip maestro bpmn instance element-executions <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
99	uip maestro bpmn instance cursors <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
100	```
101	
102	Use these to distinguish a modeling problem from a runtime-state problem:
103	
104	- Activity fault: inspect the activity's inputs, mappings, extension payload, and upstream variables.
105	- Gateway stall: inspect outgoing sequence-flow conditions, default flow, and variable values.
106	- Event wait: inspect message/timer configuration, subscriptions, and whether the expected external signal exists.
107	- Subprocess or call activity fault: identify the child dependency, but do not invoke sibling skills automatically.
108	
109	## Step 6 - Check generated package files
110	
111	If the failure is binding, entry point, package, or runtime metadata related, inspect generated JSON:
112	
113	- `bindings_v2.json`
114	- `entry-points.json`
115	- `operate.json`
116	- `package-descriptor.json`
117	
118	Generated-file mismatch usually means Author should fix BPMN or rerun CLI generation/enrichment.
119	
120	Correlate package files to the deployed BPMN:
121	
122	- `entry-points.json` should reference the intended BPMN file and start event.
123	- `bindings_v2.json` should contain generated resources required by executable resource and connector elements.
124	- `operate.json` should identify the intended main file/runtime metadata.
125	- `package-descriptor.json` should include BPMN and generated JSON files under `content/`.
126	
127	## Step 7 - Pull traces last
128	
129	Use verbose traces only when incidents, variables, deployed asset, and package files do not explain the issue.
130	
131	```bash
132	uip maestro bpmn job traces <JOB_KEY> --output json
133	```
134	
135	## Output
136	
137	Return a concise diagnosis:
138	
139	- Faulting element ID.
140	- User-visible symptom.
141	- Likely root cause.
142	- Whether the fix belongs in BPMN source, CLI enrichment, generated package files, or cloud configuration.
143	- Safe next action.
144	
145	## CLI command reference
146	
147	```bash
148	uip maestro bpmn job status <JOB_KEY> --output json
149	uip maestro bpmn job traces <JOB_KEY> --output json
150	uip maestro bpmn instance get <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
151	uip maestro bpmn instance incidents <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
152	uip maestro bpmn instance variables <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
153	uip maestro bpmn instance variables <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --parent-element-id <ELEMENT_ID> --output json
154	uip maestro bpmn instance asset <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
155	uip maestro bpmn instance element-executions <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
156	uip maestro bpmn instance cursors <INSTANCE_ID> -f <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
157	uip maestro bpmn incident get <INCIDENT_ID> --folder-key <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
158	uip maestro bpmn incident summary --output json
159	uip maestro bpmn processes incidents <PROCESS_KEY> --output json
160	```
161	
162	Lifecycle commands are intentionally absent from this diagnostic command list.
163	Use [operate/references/manage.md](../../operate/references/manage.md) only after the diagnosis supports a
164	side-effecting action and the user consents.
